'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Jane Swift]] (acting) | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mitt Romney]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsMA}} {{Mitt Romney series}} The '''2002 Massachusetts gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2002 to elect the [[Governor of Massachusetts|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Massachusetts|lieutenant governor]] of [[Massachusetts]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Jane Swift]] chose not to seek a full term in office. In the open race, Republican businessman [[Mitt Romney]] defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state treasurer [[Shannon O'Brien (Massachusetts politician)|Shannon O'Brien]] with a plurality of the vote. Primary elections were held on September 17. Romney, who was broadly popular within his party, had cleared the field early after forcing Swift to retire. O'Brien won the Democratic nomination with a third of the vote, defeating former [[United States Secretary of Labor|U.S. labor secretary]] [[Robert Reich]], [[Massachusetts Senate]] [[President of the Massachusetts Senate|president]] [[Tom Birmingham]], and former state senator [[Warren Tolman]]. Reich's campaign attracted support from progressives and leftists, but he was sharply opposed by the national party establishment for his past criticisms of former president [[Bill Clinton]]. Clinton endorsed former [[List of chairs of the Democratic National Committee|national Democratic Party chair]] [[Steven Grossman (politician)|Steve Grossman]], who ran a well-funded campaign but suffered from poor polling and withdrew from the race in July. This would be the only time Romney won a general election in the state, as in the [[2012 United States presidential election in Massachusetts|2012 presidential election]] and the [[1994 United States Senate election in Massachusetts|1994 Senate election]], he lost every county in the state. ==Republican primary== ===Governor=== ==== Candidates ==== * [[Mitt Romney]], businessman and [[1994 United States Senate election in Massachusetts|1994 U.S. Senate nominee]] =====Withdrew===== * [[Jane Swift]], acting [[governor of Massachusetts]] since 2001 (''withdrew March 19'') In 2002, Republican lieutenant governor [[Jane Swift]] was expected to campaign for the governor's office, and she had said she would in October 2001. Swift had been serving as [[acting governor]] after Republican governor [[Paul Cellucci]] resigned upon being appointed [[List of ambassadors of the United States to Canada|U.S. Ambassador to Canada]].{{Cite book|title=[[The Almanac of American Politics|The Almanac of American Politics 2004]] |last1 = Barone |first1 = Michael | author-link=Michael Barone (pundit) | first2= Richard E. | last2=Cohen | author-link2 = Richard E. Retrieved November 1, 2006. Romney was coming off a successful stint as head of the [[Salt Lake Organizing Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games of 2002|organizing committee]] for the [[2002 Winter Olympics]] in [[Salt Lake City]] and was also mentioned as a possible candidate for [[List of governors of Utah|governor of Utah]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.boston.com/news/politics/2008/specials/romney/articles/part6_main/?page=full |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007133710/http://www.boston.com/news/politics/2008/specials/romney/articles/part6_main/?page=full |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 7, 2008 |title=The Making of Mitt Romney: Part 6: Taking office, remaining an outsider |last=Mooney |first=Brian |date=June 29, 2007 |newspaper=[[The Boston Globe]]}} However, Romney had previously indicated in fall 2001 that he would not challenge a sitting Republican. Massachusetts Republican chair [[Kerry Healey]] flew to Utah to personally assess Romney's intentions. On March 17, Romney flew to Massachusetts; around that time, a ''[[Boston Herald]]'' poll showed him defeating Swift by a 75 percent to 12 percent margin in a Republican primary. Two days later, Swift declared that she had decided not to seek her party's nomination, citing family reasons and saying, "I believe that this is in the best interest of our state, as it will allow the Republican Party's best chances of holding the governor's office in November."[http://archives.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/03/19/massachusetts.governor/index.html "Swift exits, Romney joins Mass. governor's race"]{{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070813060324/http://archives.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/03/19/massachusetts.governor/index.html |date=2007-08-13 }}, [[CNN]], March 19, 2002. Retrieved October 30, 2006. Three hours later, Romney announced his candidacy. Governor's race|newspaper=Harvard Hillside|date=April 4, 2002}} Rappaport remained in the race. ==== Results ==== {{Election box begin no change | title='''Massachusetts Republican lieutenant gubernatorial primary, 2002'''}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[Kerry Healey]] |votes = 159,667 |percentage = 62.76 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[Jim Rappaport]] |votes = 88,061 |percentage = 34.62 }} {{Election box write-in with party link no change |votes = 241 |percentage = 0.09 }} {{Election box total no change |percentage = 100.00 |votes = 247,969 }} {{Election box end}} ==Democratic primary== ===Governor=== ====Candidates==== * [[Thomas Birmingham]], [[president of the Massachusetts Senate]] * [[Shannon O'Brien (Massachusetts politician)|Shannon O'Brien]], [[Treasurer and Receiver-General of Massachusetts|Massachusetts treasurer and receiver-general]] * [[Robert Reich]], former [[United States Secretary of Labor|U.S. labor secretary]] * [[Warren Tolman]], former state senator from [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] and [[1998 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|1998 lieutenant governor nominee]] =====Withdrew===== * [[Steven Grossman (politician)|Steve Grossman]], former chair of the [[Democratic National Committee|DNC]] and president of [[American Israel Public Affairs Committee|AIPAC]] The leader in most of the polls conducted was O'Brien, who was a longtime insider with four generations of heritage in the Massachusetts political establishment. However, she faced criticism for some of losing investments she had made as state treasurer. Reich's candidacy attracted considerable media attention, especially due to the 1997 publication of his memoir of working for the [[Clinton administration]], ''Locked in the Cabinet''. Reich had received criticism for embellishing events with invented dialogue, and the book had so angered [[Bill Clinton]] that he endorsed Steve Grossman in the race instead. Johnson (Independent) ** Running mate: Joe Schebel, self-employed carpenter * [[Shannon O'Brien (Massachusetts politician)|Shannon O'Brien]], [[Treasurer and Receiver-General of Massachusetts|treasurer and receiver-general of Massachusetts]] (Democratic) ** Running mate: Chris Gabrieli * [[Mitt Romney]], businessman and 1994 U.S. Senate nominee (Republican) ** Running mate: [[Kerry Healey]], former chair of the [[Massachusetts Republican Party]] * [[Jill Stein]], internist at [[Simmons University|Simmons College]] Health Center{{cite news |last=Williams |first=Eric |date=October 31, 2002 |title=Political spoiler? |newspaper=Cape Cod Times}} ([[Green-Rainbow Party|Green-Rainbow]]) ** Running mate: Tony Lorenzen, high school theology teacher ===Question of Romney's residency=== Before the primaries concluded, [[Massachusetts Democratic Party|Democratic]] officials claimed that Romney was ineligible to run for governor, citing residency issues. The [[Massachusetts Constitution]] requires that a gubernatorial candidate be an "inhabitant" for seven consecutive years prior to a run for office.[https://www.scribd.com/doc/99951135/Romney-Ballot-Law-Commission-Decision Massachusetts Ballot Law Commission Decision] (June 25, 2002) via [[Scribd]] ([http://i2.cdn.turner.com/cnn/2012/images/07/13/romney.ballot.law.commission.decision.pdf another copy] is available from the [[CNN]] [[content delivery network]]). Romney had attended business and law school at Harvard and spent his entire business career in Massachusetts until being hired to organize the Salt Lake Olympics in 1999. In 1999, Romney had listed himself as a part-time Massachusetts resident,Mcelhenny, John (Associated Press){{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130202044900/http://www.seacoastonline.com/articles/20020618-NEWS-306189981|title="Romney defends right to run for governor"}} ''Portsmouth Herald'', Tuesday, June 18, 2002. Retrieved July 12, 2012. Romney had claimed residency in [[Utah]] from 1999 to 2002, during his time as president of the Salt Lake Organizing Committee and received a $54,000 property tax break there. Romney now offered to pay back that exemption. Romney said that he had planned to return to Massachusetts all along. On June 8, 2002, the Massachusetts Democratic Party filed a complaint with the Massachusetts State Ballot Law Commission, which tended to be lenient in its interpretations of the requirements for residency.{{cite news | last = Butterfield | first = Fox | author-link = Fox Butterfield | title = Republican's Candidacy Is Challenged By Democrats | newspaper = [[The New York Times]]| date = June 8, 2002| url = https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/08/us/republican-s-candidacy-is-challenged-by-democrats.html?pagewanted=print&src=pm}} At the time the commission was composed of three Republicans, one Democrat and one independent. On June 25, 2002, the commission unanimously ruled that Romney was eligible to run for office,{{cite news | url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-120282117.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502183559/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-120282117.html | url-status=usurped | archive-date=May 2, 2013 | title=Mass. board confirms GOP gubernatorial candidate's residency | first=Evan | last=Osnos | author-link = Evan Osnos | newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] | via=[[HighBeam Research]] | url-access=subscription | location=Chicago, IL | date=June 25, 2002}} saying that "[Romney] never severed his ties to Massachusetts [and] his testimony was credible in all respects." The ruling was not challenged in court,Belluck, Pam. [https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F40911FD3C5A0C758EDDAF0894DA404482 "Massachusetts Ballot Panel Allows Race By Republican"] ''[[The New York Times]]'' (Page A-17), June 26, 2002. and Romney accused the Democrats of playing "ridiculous, dirty politics". ===Campaign=== Romney ran as a political outsider and as an agent of change, saying he would "clean up the mess on Beacon Hill."Barone and Cohen, ''The Almanac of American Politics 2004'', p. 772. He said he was "not a partisan Republican" but rather a "moderate" with "progressive" views.{{cite news | url=http://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2011/12/13/democrats-rail-against-romney-over-decade-old-comments/ | title=Democrats rail against Romney over decade-old comments | author=Killough, Ashley | publisher=CNN | date=December 13, 2011 | access-date=February 15, 2012 | archive-date=December 14, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214050837/http://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2011/12/13/democrats-rail-against-romney-over-decade-old-comments/ | url-status=dead }} See [http://motherjones.com/mojo/2011/12/romney-2002-moderate-progressive-not-partisan-Worcester "Romney in 2002: I'm 'Moderate,' 'Progressive,' and 'Not a Partisan Republican' [VIDEO]"] for video. Romney declared support for [[White House Office of Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships|faith-based initiatives]] and campaigned as a [[pro-choice]] candidate who would protect a woman's right to an [[abortion]]. He rejected the endorsement of Massachusetts Citizens for Life, an [[anti-abortion]] organization.{{Citation| last = Kessler| first = Glenn| author-link = Glenn Kessler (journalist)| title = Fact checking the CNN debate in Charleston | newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]| date = January 20, 2012| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/fact-checker/post/fact-checking-the-cnn-debate-in-charleston/2012/01/19/gIQALs8dCQ_blog.html | access-date = 2012-01-23}} O'Brien claimed Romney was "trying to mask a very conservative set of belief systems". While saying she would not criticize his membership in the [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints|Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]], she attacked his substantial donations to [[Brigham Young University]], objecting to their bar on expressions of homosexuality. O'Brien came out in support of [[same-sex marriage]]. Romney supporters hailed his business record, especially his success with the 2002 Olympics, as indicating he would be able to bring a new era of efficiency into Massachusetts politics.[https://www.pbs.org/newshour/vote2002/races/ma_governor.html "Vote 2002: Massachusetts Governor's Race"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030625184413/http://www.pbs.org/newshour/vote2002/races/ma_governor.html |date=2003-06-25 }} ''PBS Online News Hour'' (No Date). Retrieved November 1, 2006. His campaign was the first to use [[microtargeting]] techniques, in which small groups of voters were reached with narrowly tailored messaging.{{Cite news| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/07/04/AR2007070401423.html | title=Romney's Data Cruncher | author=Cillizza, Chris | author-link=Chris Cillizza | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | date=July 5, 2007}} Romney proposed to reorganize the state government and stressed his ability to obtain federal funds for the state.{{cite news |last=Karl |first=Jonathan |title=In '02 Romney touted D.C. connections, federal funds |url=https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2012/03/exclusive-in-02-romney-touted-d-c-connections-federal-funds/ |work=ABC News |date=March 2, 2012}}{{cite news|last=Isikoff |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Isikoff |title=Salt Lake City Olympics Earmarks a Double-Edged Sword for Romney |url=http://firstread.msnbc.msn.com/_news/2012/02/18/10444876-salt-lake-city-olympics-earmarks-a-double-edged-sword-for-romney?lite |work=[[NBC News]] |date=February 18, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603073730/http://firstread.msnbc.msn.com/_news/2012/02/18/10444876-salt-lake-city-olympics-earmarks-a-double-edged-sword-for-romney?lite |archive-date=June 3, 2012 }} Romney said he would cut $1 billion out of the $23 billion state budget by eliminating waste, fraud, and mismanagement while still reducing taxes over a phased period. He also said he was generally against tax increases but refused to rule out the possibility of a tax increase. He did attempt to paint O'Brien as a "[[Tax and spend|tax-and-spend]] liberal." O'Brien's campaign was hobbled by the primary, which had exhausted her campaign's time and resources. With less than two months before Election Day, she had exhausted most of her funds by spending $4.5 million to win the nomination. Romney, who had been able to focus on the general election in the absence of any primary contest, contributed over $6 million to his own campaign during the election, a state record at the time.[http://archive.boston.com/news/local/politics/candidates/articles/2006/08/22/gabrieli_surpasses_spending_record/ "Gabrieli surpasses spending record"] Brian C. Mooney ''Boston Globe''; August 22, 2006. Retrieved November 20, 2006. He also raised nearly $10 million for his campaign overall.{{cite news | url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-94133968.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129232942/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-94133968.html | url-status=usurped | archive-date=November 29, 2012 | title=Donor cash still floods campaigns | first=Ted | last=Bunker | newspaper=[[Boston Herald]] | via=HighBeam Research | url-access=subscription | date=November 11, 2002}} O'Brien focused her attacks by portraying Romney as being out of place in Massachusetts. Romney had stumbled earlier in the year by not knowing that "MCAS" stood for the [[Massachusetts Comprehensive Assessment System]] of school exams. To soften Romney's image, his campaign staged a series of "work days" over the summer, in which he performed blue-collar jobs such as herding cows, baling hay, unloading a fishing boat, and hauling garbage.{{cite news|last=Klein|first=Rick|title=New Ads, 'Work Days' Show Down-to-Earth Candidate|newspaper=The Boston Globe|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7731101.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415121048/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7731101.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=April 15, 2016|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|location=Boston, MA|date=September 26, 2002}} Also available as [https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=sVFOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pu0DAAAAIBAJ&dq=romney%20shirt-off&pg=1371%2C5073072 "Mitt takes his shirt off as campaign heats up"], ''Deseret News'', September 27, 2002. Television ads highlighting the work day effort, as well as one portraying his family in gushing terms and showing him shirtless, received a poor public response. O'Brien responded, "Massachusetts doesn't need a governor who thinks getting in touch with working people is a costume party." By mid-October, O'Brien led in most polls.{{cite news|last=Bayles|first=Fred|title=Romney may be losing his touch in Mass|url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/washington/2002-10-15-massgov-usat_x.htm|newspaper=USA Today|date=October 16, 2002}}{{cite news|last=Miga|first=Andrew|title=Don't expect a warm and fuzzy Romney this fall|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/article/20120405/PC1603/120409549|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929154441/http://www.postandcourier.com/article/20120405/PC1603/120409549|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 29, 2012|agency=Associated Press|newspaper=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=April 5, 2012}} Romney responded with negative ads that accused O'Brien of mismanaging state pension funds. One ad featured a [[Basset Hound]] sleeping as men removed bags of money from the Massachusetts treasury. Another associated her husband, former lobbyist [[Emmet Hayes]], with the [[Enron scandal]]. Jill Stein campaigned against requiring MCAS tests to graduate high school and in support of clean air and bilingual education.{{cite news |last=McConville |first=Christine |date=October 13, 2002 |title=Green Party Line Colors Governor's Race Debate |newspaper=Boston Globe}}{{cite news |last=Gitell |first=Seth |date=October 10, 2002 |title=Jill Stein won the debate |newspaper=Boston Phoenix |url=http://www.bostonphoenix.com/boston/news_features/daily/documents/02516391.htm |url-status=dead |access-date=6 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120228044605/http://www.bostonphoenix.com/boston/news_features/daily/documents/02516391.htm |archive-date=28 February 2012}} ===Debates=== In the debates, O'Brien attacked Romney repeatedly. He referred to her style as "unbecoming," which led to criticism that he was insensitive to women. After being excluded from the first debate, Stein and independent candidate Barbara Johnson sued the media organizers of the debate.{{cite web|title=Candidates Sue Media Consortium Over Debate Exclusion|url=http://www.thebostonchannel.com/news/1694291/detail.html|work=WCVB-TV Boston|publisher=Hearst Stations Inc.|access-date=6 April Superior Court]] judge Linda Giles ruled against Stein and Johnson, stating that the state's campaign finance laws did not apply to press-organized political debates and invitations to O'Brien and
